title: Vectoring pilot sequences map interposer crosstalk, enabling shieldless half-pitch HBM wiring
idea: Instrument first: borrowing DSL vectoring, each HBM PHY sends orthogonal Walsh pilot sequences on all 1024 lanes during idle slots and correlates every victim sampler against them, measuring the full neighbour coupling matrix and its thermal drift to <1% within milliseconds. With crosstalk continuously known, design an interposer with signal wires at half today's pitch and no interleaved shield tracks; each transmitter pre-subtracts predicted coupling with 4-tap neighbour precoders.
why: Facts 5-6: shields consume ~30-50% of interposer tracks; ~2x lanes per layer or half the routing layers, ~30% interposer area/cost cut, and room for wider-slower lower-pJ/bit buses; precoding costs <0.1 pJ/bit.

title: Diamond NV magnetometry images return currents, enabling ground-plane-free interposers
idea: Instrument first: a wafer-scale nitrogen-vacancy diamond film laid on a live interposer images the vector magnetic field of every signal and its return current at ~1 um resolution under real HBM traffic. Knowing exactly where return current flows, design interposers that drop continuous ground planes and co-route a measured-sufficient local return conductor beside each signal group, collapsing a 4-5 metal-layer interposer to 3 layers.
why: Capital intensity and HBM packaging cost (fact 6): each metal layer pair is ~15-20% of interposer cost; ~25-35% cheaper interposers with fewer masks, and a path to cheaper RDL interposers.

title: Nano-ohm Kelvin drift sensing lets HBM power TSVs run at triple current
idea: Instrument first: four-wire Kelvin taps on every power-TSV cluster feed an on-die chopper-stabilised integrator that detects electromigration void nucleation as a 0.05% resistance step months before failure. With that early warning, design power TSVs for ~3x JEDEC current density and let the base die steer current away from any drifting cluster via switched supply fingers, halving the power-TSV count.
why: Fact 6: power/ground TSVs are roughly half of HBM TSVs; halving them frees ~25% of TSV area for signals or smaller keep-out, cutting die area per bit by several % and enabling wider buses.

title: Toggle census remaps hot bit positions onto shortest, lowest-capacitance lanes
idea: Instrument first: per-lane transition counters in the PHY measure each bit position's toggle rate per workload phase (BF16 exponent bits toggle <5%, mantissa LSBs ~50%). A small crossbar maps bit positions to physical lanes so high-toggle bits ride the shortest, lowest-capacitance traces and quiet bits take the long ones, re-mapping whenever the census detects a phase change.
why: Fact 5: lane length/capacitance varies 2-3x across a PHY footprint; activity-matched assignment cuts I/O switching energy ~20-35% with no bandwidth, coding or protocol change.

title: Moire overlay readout selects best of three offset bond-pad phases
idea: Instrument first: moire grating pairs at every die site, read through silicon by an IR camera after bonding, report die-to-wafer overlay to ~5 nm for a whole wafer in seconds. Design hybrid-bond pads in three interleaved vernier phases offset by a third of pitch; the measured overlay fuse-selects the best-aligned phase per die, so pads can be pitched at ~0.5 um with overlay errors that would otherwise be fatal.
why: Fact 6 and capital: tolerates ~3x worse bonder overlay, letting cheaper, faster die-to-wafer bonders reach sub-um pitch; ~3x more vertical connections per mm2 for wide-slow interfaces or higher stack yield.

title: Sub-picosecond flight-time maps enable wave-pipelined, repeaterless long memory links
idea: Instrument first: vernier time-to-digital converters at both ends of every lane measure absolute flight time and its temperature and voltage coefficients to <0.5 ps continuously. With flight time known that precisely, design wave-pipelined bridge links where 4-8 bits are simultaneously in flight on a 20-30 mm transmission-line wire with no repeaters or retimers, launch times pre-skewed per lane so one shared receive clock samples all lanes.
why: Facts 5-6: lets HBM sit 20-30 mm from the GPU (more stacks per package, less thermal coupling) without SerDes; ~1 pJ/bit vs 3-5 pJ/bit for retimed long links.

title: Bond-head acoustic emission enables stop-loss stacking that caps damaged HBM stacks early
idea: Instrument first: a piezo acoustic-emission sensor and force-displacement logger in the thermocompression bond head classify every die placement live (bump-collapse signature, micro-crack bursts, edge chipping). Design a stop-loss stacking flow: when a tier is flagged, stacking halts and the partial stack is capped and sold as a lower-capacity SKU, so known-good dies are never piled onto a dead stack and dies can be thinned further.
why: Fact 6 (20-30% HBM yield loss): turns compounding per-tier loss into near-zero wasted good dies, recovering ~10-20% of DRAM die output in 12-16-high flows.

title: Embedded strain rosettes servo lid actuators to flatten 12-stack mega-packages
idea: Instrument first: piezoresistive strain rosettes built into the interposer and substrate, read through spare pins, measure package warpage live through reflow, burn-in and field thermal cycling. Design reticle-busting packages carrying 12-16 HBM stacks whose lid contains piezo or shape-memory bending actuators that servo-flatten the package to the measured strain, keeping microbumps and C4s inside their strain budget.
why: Facts 5-6: warpage caps package size near 3-4 reticles; active flattening could allow ~2x more HBM per accelerator and avoid premium low-CTE cores and stiffeners.

title: Traffic-matrix telemetry, then antifuse burn-in of interposer lane allocation
idea: Instrument first: on-interposer probes log the logic-to-memory traffic matrix (per chiplet, channel, read/write mix) while the customer's real workload runs during burn-in. A passive interposer with antifuse cross-connects is then permanently configured, reallocating lanes among HBM stacks, CXL ports and chiplet links to match the measured matrix (e.g. read-heavy inference vs balanced training).
why: Facts 5-6: provisioning for measured rather than worst-case traffic lets ~20-30% fewer PHY lanes deliver the same effective bandwidth, cutting beachfront and pJ/bit; one interposer SKU serves many products.

title: Per-TSV C-V sweeps enable bias-depleted liners cutting TSV capacitance 40%
idea: Instrument first: an on-die capacitance-to-digital converter sweeps each TSV's MOS liner C-V curve (oxide charge, flat-band, local doping) inside the finished stack. Design TSVs set in a lightly doped annulus with a separately biased substrate ring that holds every liner in deep depletion at the measured per-cluster optimum, shrinking TSV capacitance from ~50 fF to ~30 fF.
why: Facts 5-6: TSV charging dominates vertical pJ/bit; ~40% lower capacitance gives ~40% lower TSV energy and faster edges, or permits thinner liners and smaller TSVs.

title: Live bond-resistance endpointing ends hybrid-bond anneals early and cool
idea: Instrument first: eddy-current coils and daisy-chain taps in the anneal chuck track Cu-Cu bond formation (resistance falling as asperities close) wafer by wafer in real time. Design a hybrid-bonding flow for DRAM tiers that stops each anneal at measured completion, often 200-250 C for minutes instead of a fixed 350-400 C for hours, protecting access-transistor retention and capacitor dielectric.
why: Facts 3 and 6: avoids ~10-30% retention degradation from bonding anneals and raises anneal throughput 3-5x; enables bonding heat-sensitive memory tiers.

title: Micro pressure-sensing film maps bond force, enabling single-press 16-die stacking
idea: Instrument first: a reusable microcapsule pressure-sensing film with ~10 um resolution, placed in a dummy stack, reports the force map of a gang-bonding press, and per-position compliant shims are laser-cut to flatten it. Design an HBM line that stacks all 16 dies with non-conductive film in place and bonds them in one thermocompression cycle instead of 16 sequential bonds.
why: Fact 6 and capital: ~10x fewer bonder-hours per stack, fewer thermal cycles on lower tiers (higher yield), and lower capital per HBM unit, key to onshoring HBM assembly.

title: Real-time VPP telemetry lets one base-die pump feed every tier
idea: Instrument first: each DRAM die streams its VPP/VBB load current and droop at sub-us resolution over a dedicated TSV, revealing the stack-level coincidence statistics of activations. Design HBM core dies with no charge pumps: one high-efficiency inductive boost on the base die supplies VPP to all tiers through shared TSVs, sized to the measured coincidence profile rather than eight worst cases.
why: Facts 7 and 10: pumps and their decap take several % of each die and run at ~30-40% efficiency; removing 7 of 8 pumps saves ~3-5% die area per tier and ~20% of wordline-supply energy.

title: Rail-ripple demodulators let commands ride on stack power TSVs
idea: Instrument first: on-die chopper demodulators measure supply-rail ripple at the uV level and lock to a pilot tone the base die injects onto the stack power rails. Design HBM stacks where command, die-select and mode-register traffic travel as low-amplitude OFDM tones on the power TSVs (power-line communication inside the stack), eliminating dedicated command/address TSVs with their drivers and ESD.
why: Facts 6-7: frees ~5-10% of signal TSVs and their periphery; command bandwidth is only ~1-2 Gb/s per channel, which in-stack power-line signalling can carry.

title: Captured pulse responses enable duobinary partial-response signalling on interposers
idea: Instrument first: an on-die sampler sweeps phase across repeated isolated pulses to capture each lane's complete single-bit response in situ. Design interposer links that deliberately run at ~2x the channel's -3 dB bandwidth using duobinary partial-response shaping fitted to the measured response, so ISI becomes a known three-level code decoded by a comparator pair instead of noise to be equalised away.
why: Facts 5-6: ~2x bits per lane at similar energy, halving lane count or interposer layers for a given bandwidth and making cheaper RDL interposers usable.

title: Cloud bills metered picojoules moved, pricing data movement explicitly
idea: Instrument first: counters in memory controllers, HBM PHYs and CXL switches attribute measured energy per byte moved to each tenant and process, calibrated by replica-charge sensing in the PHY. The business: clouds bill data movement as its own line item and publish locality discounts, so customers fuse kernels, tile and quantize KV to cut HBM traffic, raising usable bandwidth and capacity per GPU.
why: Fact 5: movement is 20-25% of accelerator power; a price signal could cut fleet memory traffic ~15-30%, deferring HBM purchases during the shortage.

title: Per-wire inductance metering plus on-die trim makes wire-bonded stacks run fast
idea: Instrument first: at final test each die's I/O pad measures its own bond-wire inductance and loop resonance with an on-die frequency sweep, then a per-pad programmable capacitor and peaking network is trimmed to the measured value, turning each wire into a matched flat-response channel. Design TSV-free, spacer-separated wire-bonded 8-16-die stacks of commodity DRAM running 6-8 Gb/s per pin for HBM-like capacity per footprint.
why: Fact 6: avoids the ~3x wafer-area-per-bit TSV tax and TSV yield loss, using commodity dies and mature U.S. OSAT wire bonders.

title: On-pad ESD event recorders prove die-to-die I/O can drop ESD diodes
idea: Instrument first: tiny charge-integrating recorders with fuse latches on each microbump and hybrid-bond pad log every electrostatic discharge event and its energy through wafer handling, bonding and stacking. With field data showing bonded die-to-die pads see only events far below standard ratings, design HBM and chiplet I/O with ESD protection cut ~10x, or removed on bond-only pads, slashing pad capacitance.
why: Fact 5: ESD is ~30-50% of a short-reach pad's capacitance; removing it cuts I/O energy ~30% and pad area, enabling finer bond pitch.

title: In-situ PDN impedance chirps let schedulers dodge resonance, halving decap
idea: Instrument first: on-die current-sink chirps sweep 1 MHz-1 GHz and measure the HBM stack's power-delivery impedance in situ, tracking resonance peaks as temperature and aging shift them. The memory controller then shapes burst and activation repetition rates so the traffic current spectrum carries notches at the measured peaks, allowing on-die and interposer decoupling capacitance to be roughly halved.
why: Fact 7: decap is a significant periphery and base-die area item; ~5% die area returned plus ~30-50 mV less supply guardband for I/O energy.

title: A pJ-per-useful-bit benchmark standard steers memory procurement
idea: Instrument first: an open metrology standard and reference fixture that measures energy per useful bit delivered (counting overfetch, refresh, retraining and idle) on recorded AI and database traces, published per memory SKU like an efficiency label. Federal and hyperscaler procurement then buys on measured pJ/useful-bit and effective GB, rewarding interfaces that cut overfetch and movement rather than raw GB/s.
why: Facts 5 and 8: aligns market incentives with the ~5.9 pJ/useful-bit problem, steering design toward 2-3x lower movement energy per useful bit.

title: In-package alpha counters let memory use ordinary, non-low-alpha solder
idea: Instrument first: reverse-biased silicon diode arrays in the base die count actual alpha-particle hits and energies inside each package in the field. Design packages that use standard solders, mold fillers and underfills instead of specialty low-alpha refined materials, with ECC scrub cadence and spare remapping set from each package's measured flux rather than an assumed worst case.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: low-alpha tin, lead and refined fillers are niche concentrated supply chains; removes a chokepoint and ~1-3% package material cost with measured soft-error margins.

title: Base-die retention ledger turns unrefreshed DRAM into a write-back cache over MRAM
idea: Instrument first: at assembly the base die measures every row's retention at three temperatures through the TSVs and stores a per-row Arrhenius fit; in operation it timestamps each row write and integrates on-die temperature into a decay clock. Design: DRAM tiers are never refreshed; the base die writes dirty rows back to an in-stack MRAM tier before their measured deadline and silently invalidates clean ones, giving DRAM-speed access with zero refresh power.
why: Fact 3: eliminates the ~46 fJ/bit refresh, 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss; most AI tensors are overwritten or dead within seconds, so write-back traffic is small.

title: Measured per-row flip curves let error-tolerant tensors live in refresh-off DRAM
idea: Instrument first: an in-stack tester measures each row's bit-flip probability versus time-since-write and temperature (a full decay curve, not a pass/fail bin). The allocator places error-tolerant data (activations, gradients, low-precision KV) in refresh-disabled rows whose measured flip probability at the data's expected lifetime is below 1e-6, sign and exponent bits in the strongest rows, while long-lived weights sit in a non-volatile tier: no row is ever refreshed.
why: Fact 3: zero refresh power for the dominant transient data class; flip rates below 1e-6 sit under the noise ML training already tolerates.

title: Per-array retention-voltage census lets stacked SRAM tiers hold at 0.3 V
idea: Instrument first: each SRAM array on a 28-40 nm die measures its own data-retention voltage by stepping the hold rail down against canary rows, logging a per-array DRV map (typically 0.2-0.35 V versus a 0.7 V guardband). Design an HBM-substitute stack of 8-12 hybrid-bonded mature-node SRAM dies whose idle arrays each sit at their measured DRV plus 30 mV: static, refresh-free working memory with ~5-10x lower standby leakage.
why: Zero refresh; mature U.S. fabs, no EUV (facts 4, capital); standby power competitive with DRAM refresh plus background; supply not tied to DRAM fabs.

title: In-situ thermal-stability metrology lets MRAM tiers bond directly onto hot GPUs
idea: Instrument first: MTJ test cells across each die measure thermal-stability factor (switching-field distribution) and local stray field under the GPU's real power map at operating temperature. Design MRAM tiers hybrid-bonded straight onto the logic die with region-graded MTJ stacks (high-stability over hotspots, fast-write elsewhere) and shielding only where measured fields demand it: non-volatile, refresh-free capacity with no HBM PHY.
why: Zero refresh; removes PHY and interposer (fact 5: 3-4 pJ/bit to <0.5 pJ/bit); DRAM on 90-105 C logic would need doubled refresh, MRAM needs none.

title: Package-embedded bias magnets, Hall-mapped per die, enable field-assisted SOT-MRAM tiers
idea: Instrument first: Hall-sensor arrays on a calibration die map, to about 2 Oe, the in-plane field from a thin rare-earth-free (MnBi or ferrite) magnet layer laminated into the package lid. Design spin-orbit-torque MRAM tiers that rely on this measured uniform bias for deterministic ~1 ns switching, so MTJ stacks skip complex field-free exchange layers; bits are non-volatile and need zero refresh.
why: Zero refresh with unlimited-endurance sub-ns SOT writes; simpler MTJ stacks cut process steps; rare-earth-free magnets avoid a China chokepoint.

title: On-die write-error metering lets MRAM fire short pulses, retrying over links
idea: Instrument first: each MRAM bank measures its live write-error rate versus pulse width with a read-after-write comparator and keeps a histogram. The interface protocol then writes with aggressively short, low-current pulses tuned to a measured ~1e-3 error rate, verifies in the background and retries only failed words via a link-level NACK, instead of guard-banded 1e-9 pulses.
why: Zero refresh (non-volatile cells) plus ~3-5x lower write energy and ~2x write bandwidth, closing MRAM's main gap to DRAM in the working-memory role.

title: Hard-disk read-head fabs build MTJ memory layers for bonding to base dies
idea: Instrument first: hard-disk head fabs already run wafer-level TMR and coercivity probers measuring millions of tunnel junctions per wafer; extend them to qualify dense MTJ arrays. Strategy: these existing head fabs pattern passive MTJ-plus-selector arrays that are hybrid-bonded onto CMOS periphery base dies from mature logic fabs, yielding zero-refresh non-volatile working-memory stacks without a DRAM fab.
why: Capital intensity and U.S./allied manufacturability: reuses under-utilised head-fab capacity (HDD unit volumes falling) for tens of $M retrofits rather than $15B fabs; zero refresh.

title: Lock-in anomalous-Hall readout unlocks field-immune antiferromagnetic memory beside power TSVs
idea: Instrument first: on-die lock-in readout amplifiers resolve the ~0.1% anomalous-Hall resistance change of antiferromagnetic (Mn3Sn-type) bits at ns timescales, a signal too small for normal sense amps. Design antiferromagnetic memory tiers packed directly around power TSVs and inductors, where stray fields forbid MRAM, switched by current pulses in tens of ps, non-volatile and refresh-free.
why: Zero refresh; field immunity removes shielding and allows densest placement in high-current zones; ultrafast switching; no rare-earths.

title: In-situ gap capacitance metrology enables NEMS-gated vacuum capacitors in interposers
idea: Instrument first: each nanoelectromechanical access switch's gap and contact state is read by attofarad capacitive displacement sensing at wafer test, screening stiction and setting per-row actuation voltages. Design interposer-BEOL memory where each bit is charge on a sealed vacuum-gap capacitor accessed by a NEMS switch with no semiconductor junction, so off-leakage is effectively zero and charge persists for days: refresh-free buffer memory in a passive interposer line.
why: Fact 3: removes the junction-leakage tail that forces refresh (zero refresh); built with interposer/BEOL tools and no front-end; ~10 ns mechanical switching.

title: Pull-out voltage census enables NEMS adhesion latches inside TSV keep-out zones
idea: Instrument first: a pull-in/pull-out voltage sweep measured per relay through the array maps each nanorelay's adhesion hysteresis window. Design bistable contact latches, where the bit is whether a beam is held to an electrode by calibrated adhesion, fabricated in the otherwise wasted TSV keep-out zones of HBM dies, held at zero power and read by contact conductance as refresh-free tag, ECC and metadata memory.
why: Zero refresh; reclaims keep-out area (fact 6: several % of die) for static storage that offloads metadata from refreshed arrays.

title: Kerr-imaged domain-wall pinning calibrates racetrack chiplets for streaming weights
idea: Instrument first: a magneto-optical Kerr microscope images every racetrack's domain-wall motion under test current pulses, mapping pinning sites and per-track velocity, and the shift-pulse recipe for each track is fused into the controller. Design non-volatile racetrack chiplets whose sequential shift-out matches inference weight streaming, delivering weights over a short bridge at ~1 pJ/bit with zero refresh.
why: Zero refresh; racetracks promise ~4-10x MRAM density, and sequential access sidesteps DRAM's 128x row overfetch (fact 8).

title: In-bonder hysteresis tracing keeps ferroelectric memory tiers below imprint during bonding
idea: Instrument first: test capacitors wired to the bond chuck are pulsed throughout hybrid bonding and anneal, tracing their polarization loop (remanence, coercive shift) live so the thermal and pressure profile stops before imprint or wake-up loss sets in. Design HZO 1T1C ferroelectric tiers hybrid-bonded into HBM-like stacks under these measured-safe recipes: non-volatile, zero-refresh capacity tiers.
why: Zero refresh; bonding thermal budget is a known killer of ferroelectric margin, and live loop tracing makes stacked ferroelectric tiers manufacturable.

title: Attofarad dielectric sensing reads ferroelectric cells without destroying them
idea: Instrument first: base-die sense amps measure the small-signal capacitance of each ferroelectric capacitor, which differs several percent between polarization states because of the asymmetric C-V butterfly, using an attofarad charge-balance bridge. Design a non-destructive-read ferroelectric tier: reads never switch polarization, so read endurance is unlimited, no restore write is needed, and storage needs zero refresh.
why: Zero refresh; removes ferroelectric destructive read and read-driven fatigue, decisive for read-dominated AI traffic (fact 8 analogue).

title: RF-filter fabs build AlScN ferroelectric-diode memory chiplets
idea: Instrument first: RF bulk-acoustic-wave filter fabs already map AlScN piezo coefficient and coercive field wafer-wide with resonance probers; adapt them to map remanent-polarization uniformity. Strategy: these fabs sputter AlScN ferroelectric-diode crosspoint arrays (resistive, non-destructive read, years of retention) that are bonded onto mature-node periphery dies as zero-refresh working-memory chiplets.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: uses existing U.S. BAW filter lines and sputter tools, no EUV or DRAM fab; zero refresh; BEOL-temperature compatible.

title: SHG-imaged domain walls let one LiNbO3 interposer film host modulators and memory
idea: Instrument first: second-harmonic-generation microscopy images ferroelectric domain walls in thin-film lithium niobate non-destructively across whole wafers. Design a photonic interposer whose thin-film LiNbO3 layer hosts both electro-optic modulators and conductive-domain-wall memory cells (wall present means low resistance, read non-destructively), giving a non-volatile, zero-refresh buffer co-located with optical I/O.
why: Zero refresh; amortises an expensive film already present for optics; domain walls switch in ns, putting buffering beside the link without DRAM.

title: Generation-lifetime metrology qualifies SiC charge-storage chiplets from power-device fabs
idea: Instrument first: pulsed MOS-capacitor (Zerbst) generation-lifetime mapping across SiC wafers certifies thermal generation rates so low that stored charge decays over hours to years. Design 1T1C charge-storage memory chiplets built in SiC power-device fabs, where the 3.3 eV bandgap makes junction leakage negligible, giving refresh-free DRAM-like cells connected to the host over a short bridge.
why: Zero refresh (fact 3 leakage tail eliminated by bandgap); uses existing U.S. SiC fab capacity instead of $15B DRAM capex; density is lower but supply is domestic.

title: Factory-measured delay tables let memory PHYs skip all periodic retraining
idea: Instrument first: at wafer test every lane's delay, offset and impedance are measured across a voltage-temperature grid by on-die TDCs and stored as compact polynomial tables in the PHY's own fuses. Paired with a static or non-volatile memory tier, design a subsystem whose PHY runs open-loop from on-die thermometers, with no periodic ZQ calibration, strobe retraining or keep-alive toggling, so nothing refreshes, neither cells nor links.
why: Zero refresh power extended to the interface: periodic recalibration and keep-alive cost ~5-10% of idle I/O power and stall traffic; enables instant wake from deep sleep.

title: Write-intensity meters migrate pages between SRAM and MRAM tiers, eliminating DRAM
idea: Instrument first: per-page write-rate counters in the base die (a few bits per 4 KB, sketch-based) measure write intensity continuously. Design a DRAM-free stack where an SRAM tier absorbs write-hot pages and an MRAM tier holds everything else; pages migrate when measured write rate crosses a threshold set by MRAM write energy and endurance, so neither tier ever refreshes and MRAM endurance becomes effectively unlimited.
why: Zero refresh; MRAM-class density with SRAM-class write behaviour; endurance solved architecturally as the brief allows.

title: In-situ B-H loop tracing revives microfabricated magnetic-core memory in substrates
idea: Instrument first: each micro-toroid's B-H hysteresis loop is traced in situ through its sense winding by pulse-response flux measurement, setting per-plane drive currents. Design thin-film permalloy or ferrite toroids electroplated inside an organic package substrate and threaded by plated vias and RDL lines (X, Y, sense), forming non-volatile core-memory planes beneath the logic die with zero refresh.
why: Zero refresh; made in substrate and PCB fabs (U.S.-capable) with no front-end; ~50-100 ns for small cores suits buffers and metadata.

title: Metallic-tube census enables monolithic carbon-nanotube SRAM tiers on HBM base dies
idea: Instrument first: an in-line electrical breakdown-and-measure step identifies every metallic nanotube in each transistor channel by current-voltage census, burns them out and logs per-cell quality. Design sub-400 C CNT-FET SRAM tiers built monolithically on top of the HBM or logic base die, giving several stacked layers of static, refresh-free memory with no bonding step.
why: Zero refresh; monolithic 3D static memory without wafer bonding, at BEOL temperatures in existing U.S. foundry lines.

title: Microthermometry-held VO2 cells store bits in GPU waste-heat hysteresis
idea: Instrument first: dense on-package microthermometers map each memory region's temperature so every VO2 cell is parked inside its measured insulator-metal hysteresis window (~5-8 K wide near 65 C), held there by GPU waste heat rather than electrical power. Design bistable VO2 memory: a short Joule pulse writes the metallic state, a gate-field or local Peltier pulse writes the insulating state, and resistance reads non-destructively, with zero refresh and zero hold power.
why: Zero refresh; retention powered by heat the package must already remove; VO2 switches in ns.
